top.title: Fed Revamps Bank Stress Tests: What Does it Mean for U.S. Banks?
top.summary: The Federal Reserve has finalized revisions to its annual bank stress-testing framework aimed at increasing transparency and reducing volatility in capital requirements. Starting in 2028, stress capital buffers (SCBs) will be calculated using two-year averages of supervisory stress tests, potentially reducing year-over-year volatility by roughly 50%. While this should provide major banks with greater visibility for capital planning, the changes are unlikely to result in broad-based capital relief, with benefits varying by institution based on trading exposure and fee-income composition.

top.title: Fed Revamps Bank Stress Tests: What Does it Mean for U.S. Banks?
top.summary: The Federal Reserve has finalized revisions to its annual bank stress-testing framework aimed at increasing transparency and reducing volatility in capital requirements. Starting in 2028, stress capital buffers (SCBs) will be calculated using two-year averages of supervisory stress tests, potentially reducing year-over-year volatility by roughly 50%. top.title: Fed Revamps Bank Stress Tests: What Does it Mean for U.S. Banks?
top.summary: The Federal Reserve has finalized revisions to its annual bank stress-testing framework aimed at increasing transparency and reducing volatility in capital requirements. Starting in 2028, stress capital buffers (SCBs) will be calculated using two-year averages of supervisory stress tests, potentially reducing year-over-year volatility by roughly 50%. While this should provide major banks with greater visibility for capital planning, the changes are unlikely to result in broad-based capital relief, with benefits varying by institution based on trading exposure and fee-income composition.

top.title: Is LUNR Building a Full-Service Space Infrastructure Platform?

top.summary: Silexion Therapeutics announced the first patient has been successfully dosed in its Phase 2/3 clinical trial of SIL204, an RNAi therapy for locally advanced pancreatic cancer with KRAS mutations. The study includes an initial safety cohort of ~18 patients followed by expansion to ~166 patients across Israel and Germany.
